title: When the Current Breaks
premise: Ines Montrose, a mountain guide erased from two countries' registries after a disaster they may or may not have caused, is salvaging a quiet living on the Rimewater when the river drops a sealed chest at their feet—stamped with the crest of Vessia, a drowned nation everyone pretends never existed. The chest contains proof that Ines's own family helped sink Vessia, and inside it a map to the wreck of the flagship where the rest of the archive lies. Hunted by a salvage fleet backed by the government that blacklisted them, and shadowed by a Vessian descendant who wants the truth published rather than sold, Ines must decide whether loyalty to their dead family outweighs the truth that could restore their name. They race the fleet downriver through six tides as the dry season drains the waterways, reaching the wreck with hours to spare. Ines floods the archive's location to keep it from both sides—but keeps one page, choosing truth over inheritance and finally facing the disaster that ruined them.
about_author: Noor Halloran is a former river surveyor who spent six seasons mapping waterways that no longer appear on official charts. Their fiction blends hard-edged survival detail with questions of who gets remembered and who gets erased.

chapters.title: What the River Returns
chapters.summary: Ines Montrose, guiding a timid client down the Rimewater under a false permit, spots the chest wedged in a flood-scoured snag. POV: Ines. The beat is wary curiosity—the wilderness has given them something for the first time in years, and Ines knows gifts from rivers are never free.

chapters.title: The Seal of a Drowned Country
chapters.summary: Ines pries the chest open alone: Vessian documents, a half-melted map, and letters bearing their grandmother's name. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: vertigo—the identity they built after exile suddenly rests on a nation history insists was never real.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: A harbor contact warns that the Corvane salvage fleet has charter papers for the same stretch, and the dry season will drop the channels below navigable depth in twelve days. POV: Ines. Beat: cold arithmetic—Ines counts tides, supplies, and enemies, and decides to run the river ahead of the fleet.

chapters.title: The Passenger Who Knew Too Much
chapters.summary: Ines takes on a paying passenger, Teo Vasq, who reveals himself as a Vessian descendant hunting the same archive—not for money but for publication. POV: alternating Ines/Teo. Beat: uneasy alliance; each recognizes the other is lying about something.

chapters.title: Port of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Resupplying at a smuggler port, Ines learns the fleet has bought the harbormaster and that their old guide partner, Sefa, is piloting for Corvane. POV: Ines. Beat: betrayal sharpened by guilt—Sefa was the other survivor of the disaster that got Ines blacklisted.

chapters.title: The Gorge of Names
chapters.summary: Ines runs an uncharted gorge at night to lose the fleet, nearly drowning, saved by Teo's quick rigging. POV: Ines. Beat: grudging trust hardens into loyalty—and Ines admits, almost aloud, what really happened on the mountain years ago.

chapters.title: Sefa's Price
chapters.summary: Sefa intercepts Ines at a deadfall camp, offering to falsify the fleet's charts if Ines surrenders the chest—Corvane holds her debts. POV: Sefa. Beat: mirrored damage; two people ruined by the same lie, each convinced the other chose wrong.

chapters.title: Low Water
chapters.summary: Tide five: the channel shallows faster than predicted, forcing Ines to abandon the boat and haul the chest overland while the fleet's gunboats close from behind. POV: Teo. Beat: desperation and resolve—Teo realizes Ines plans to destroy the archive, not sell or share it.

chapters.title: The Wreck of the Meridian Star
chapters.summary: At the drained lakebed, Ines reaches the flagship's exposed hull first and opens the archive vault as the fleet arrives. Confronting Sefa and the Corvane captain, Ines detonates the scuttling charges, collapsing the wreck and archive into the flooding channel. POV: Ines. Beat: climax—choosing truth over treasure, and over inheritance.

chapters.title: One Page
chapters.summary: Ines and Teo drift out on the last tide with a single page: the letter proving Ines's grandmother tried to stop the sinking. Ines sends it to a journalist, ending their invisibility on purpose. POV: Ines. Beat: resolution—identity reclaimed not through innocence but through testimony, as the dry season closes the river behind them.
